newsitem.title: FINLAND: Orion seeks European OK for entacapone.
newsitem.headline: Orion seeks European OK for entacapone.

text.p: Finnish pharmaceuticals group Orion said in a statement on Monday it had sought marketing approval for entacapone, a Parkinson's drug, from the European Agency for the Evaluation of Medicinal Products (EMEA).
"Entacapone belongs to a new class of Parkinson's disease (PD) medicines called COMT inhibitors," it said.

The drug increases the amount of dopamine that reaches the brain, "a basic challenge in Parkinson's Disease treatment" and clinical data have shown this action increases patients' daily "on time", reducing motor fluctuations, Orion said.

Orion has an international licence, distribution and marketing agreement with Novartis for the drug, giving Orion rights to the Scandinavian and Baltic countries, sharing it in some other European countries and putting other European countries and the rest of the world in Novartis' control.
Orion said COMT inhibitors could ease the symptoms of Parkinson's Disease, suffered by about four million people worldwide.
